text:
Ben A: Quick sync idea: propose a low-downtime per-component rotation flow for on-prem / air-gapped installs. Working name: 'freezeback' (freeze, stage, swap, verify, rollback). Thoughts?

Maria (infra): Nice. Main concern is compatibility across components (lib/ABI mismatches) when we stagger swaps. We need a small compatibility manifest and a preflight graph check.

Jamal (ops): Ops constraint: rollback must be fast (<10m) for critical nodes. Suggest steps: prebake snapshot, stage into /.staged/<component>, validate, symlink flip, health restart. Example: `rdu admin rotate --component runtime --target v1.2.3 --dry-run`

Sylvia (eng-runtime): Strong +1 for sidecar staging and atomic symlink flip. Never overwrite GPU libs in-place. Also require loader to accept dual-path config while transitioning.

Drew (sre): Canary idea: try on 3 seats, observe 5m. If stable, ramp per-rack. Also take a filesystem snapshot before swap (so rollback can restore exact state).

Ben A: Draft playbook: 1) freeze inbound for target subset (conn-proxy redirect) 2) stage component (sidecar or /.staged) 3) run smoke and perf probes (`curl /health && ./probe perf`) 4) atomically flip pointer 5) monitor 5m 6) if fail -> `freezeback rollback` restores pointer + restart

deploy-bot: sandbox run scheduled: 2024-08-22T15:00Z (ops notified) :calendar:

Maria (infra): Snapshot metadata should be standard: keys: component, revision, sha256, abi_tag, signed. Use name pattern `snapshot-<comp>-<rev>-<sha>` to make GC/prune predictable.

Jamal (ops): Disk-constrained nodes with large shards are tricky. Options: a) stream-activate (download-on-activate), b) attach external shadow-cache, c) partial activation w/ loader fallback. We should document fallback tradeoffs.

Sylvia (eng-runtime): For air-gapped installs signing is mandatory. Operator must run `rdu verify --sig staged/snapshot-...` before activation. Verification must be part of the activation contract.

Ben A: Another pattern: lazy-activation: stage blobs fully but only flip the activation pointer at the end. Minimizes activation downtime for large artifacts.

Drew (sre): Important: single source-of-truth for activation state. Make operator own the activation commit and use leader election. Avoid split-state races.

Maria (infra): GC policy: default unreferenced snapshot TTL = 24h. Admin override allowed. Provide `prune --dry-run` for audits.

Jamal (ops): Will run dry-run next week on air-gapped testbed and record staging/activation/rollback timings.

Sylvia (eng-runtime): I'll review the operator contract and define compatibility checks (abi matrix, minimal api probes).

Drew (sre): Capture metrics during dry-run: staging_time, activation_time, rollback_time, peak_disk_usage, latency_delta. We'll use to set canary windows.

Ben A: Example minimal manifest we can standardize (as a single-line JSON blob in the manifest list): {"component":"runtime","rev":"v1.2.3","sha256":"abc123...","abi":"cuda12.1","signed":"true"}

Ben A: I'll write an RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams and the k8s operator stage/activate/rollback API. Reviewers: @Sylvia @Drew?

Sylvia (eng-runtime): On it. Will check compatibility matrix and operator hooks. :thumbsup:

Jamal (ops): I'll post timing numbers once I run the dry-run.

Drew (sre): Add watchdog timers into the operator so long-running activations auto-fail into rollback path.

Ben A: Great. I'll post the RFC link when ready. Thanks all.
